axis: J / partial benefit beyond the integrated stress response: glial reactivity

mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class
mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Held at abstention: the sign of the glial difference is not the same in the two species measured, no glial arm exists in any WWOX system after a drug, and the time order of gliosis and seizures was never measured in the same animals.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery

disease_assertions.measured_result_note: Microglial markers are at or near zero (P2RY12, CX3CR1, PTPRC, TREM2; these are microglial or myeloid markers, PTPRC being a pan-leukocyte marker, which is general knowledge and not settled by a held source; AIF1 and CD68 are detectable at 3.8 to 14.6 and 8.8 to 38 CPM) so the tissue cannot test a microglial arm; of seven reactive-pan genes above 5 counts (the unit is counts; SERPINA3 is 0.4 to 3 CPM and C3 1.5 to 7.6 CPM) only VIM and CD44 are raised (a radial-glia or progenitor association of the two is not stated in a held source; one reader's check of an unperturbed cortical spheroid time course from another laboratory, GSE150123, found CD44 rising with culture age, rho +0.92, recomputed by a second blind reader), SERPINA3, TIMP1 and SOCS3 are lower, C3 is not separated, and STAT3 is higher in all four knockout libraries (1.46 times, in the authors' up list, adjusted P 5.74E-03) but below the 1.5-fold cut of the declared rule; IL1B, IL6, TNF are not informative (under 20 raw counts). GFAP RNA is not raised (ratio 0.88; median-of-ratios 0.84; in neither list) and the article's week-15 qPCR for GFAP is flat (by eye about 1.1 against 1.0, no mark, n 4 v 4, one batch), while S100B and AQP4 are higher at week 15 (by eye about 2.7 and 2.4, one asterisk). The week-15 GFAP immunofluorescence (Fig 3A) is one unquantified representative field per genotype, by eye somewhat brighter in the knockout, and S100beta is the clearer difference. The authors write that GFAP also marks radial glia at week 15; GFAP rises clearly only later (week-24 qPCR, by eye about 26-fold; immunoblot at week 20 or 24). So at week 15 RNA and the qPCR are flat for GFAP and the protein evidence is weak, not clearly higher. Not a gliosis measurement and not myelin or seizure evidence.

p4_card.identity: Glial-reactivity modulators as a class: IL-1 axis agents (an IL-1 receptor antagonist, IL-1beta antibodies, caspase-1 and NLRP3 inhibitors), JAK-STAT inhibitors, tetracycline-class microglial modulators. No compound is carded; the card exists to record what the WWOX record does and does not let this class be aimed at.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF glial reactivity is (a) real in a seizing WWOX brain, (b) not just a seizure consequence that would resolve with seizure control and (c) causally harmful rather than protective. None of the three is established. Every precedent is from acute or acquired inflammation in a normally developing brain; the WWOX lesion is congenital and neuron-intrinsic.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: New in this cycle: (1) the rat and mouse glial signs conflict and the authors of the rat paper say so; the rat deficit is present from the first age measured (PND 5, about half of wild type), before the strain's sound-evoked seizures (after PND 16, no EEG), while the null mouse excess is read at P14 to P20, after seizure onset (neuron-restricted deletion: from P9; null: within a few days after birth, per Repudi 2021; recordings in the AAV paper begin at about P14): no study in the P10 reading set (the papers read for the P10 cycle, listed in partial_benefit_it6_p10_20261029) was found that reads glia and EEG in the same animals over the days that bracket onset. (2) Microglia carry no detectable Wwox in the rat; the astroglial conditional deletion was scored only for delay, weight and survival. (3) In the deposited week-15 organoid transcripts (4 v 2 libraries; no microglia, no behavioural seizures) no reactive-astrocyte programme appears, whereas the source paper reports higher GFAP and S100B by immunofluorescence at weeks 15 and 24 (GFAP also marks radial glia): an assay and marker difference, not a settled absence. (4) The deposited thresholded tables of the P47T mouse do not list Gfap, Aif1, Il1b, Tnf, Il6 or Lcn2: the regulator-level inflammatory inference there does not rest on those canonical transcripts (absence from a thresholded list is not a measurement). [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-239: in the repository re-run, the hallmark TNFA/NF-kB gene-set enrichment rests on one or two animals: without mutants M6 and F8 it meets positive-direction q < 0.05 in no forebrain region, and in cortex removing M6 alone reverses its enrichment score.] (5) The need's compound list could not reach the two IL-1-axis agents that have epilepsy exposure, because their targets (the IL-1 receptor and caspase-1) were not on the need.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: needs.json NEED-NEUROINFLAMMATION-GLIA; map R-06 and M10; HYP-20260705-02 (JAK2/STAT3 bridge, id only); DL-REPO-002.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE if ever; the first use of this thread is as a readout (is gliosis a seizure-independent early marker?), the lever question follows only if the answer is yes.
p4_card.mechanism: Target (if pursued): IL1R1, IL1B, CASP1, NLRP3, JAK2 and STAT3 in glia. Direction wanted: less reactive-glia signalling, only if the cause-versus-consequence experiment says glia are upstream of any measured harm. The causal compartment of the phenotype is neuronal (neuron-restricted deletion reproduces it, neuron-restricted gene replacement reverses it), so a glial drug is not expected to touch the cause.

external_not_wwox_evidence: Giussani 2025 (PMID 40614647), anakinra in cryptogenic NORSE/FIRES, 14 patients, abstract only
Feng 2025 (PMID 40481521), minocycline in chronic FIRES, three patients, abstract only
Chen 2026 (PMID 42111266), review of pyroptosis in epilepsy: VX-765 phase II did not meet its primary efficacy endpoint, abstract only
Galanopoulou 2017 (PMID 28462453), VX-765 without effect in a rat infantile-spasms model, abstract only
Genin 2026 (PMID 41841337), Scn1a+/- mouse: astroglial GFAP rises from disease aggravation (PN20-35) against a presymptomatic earlier time point, abstract only
Bedner 2015 (PMID 25765328), astrocyte uncoupling precedes seizures in a mouse model of temporal-lobe epilepsy, abstract only
Hristova 2016 (PMID 26669927), STAT3 deletion or JAK2 inhibition reduce glial activation and damage in neonatal hypoxia-ischaemia, abstract only
Hanin 2024 (PMID 38430119), pooled review of second-line immunotherapy in NORSE/FIRES, 75 patients, abstract only

for: Gliosis is raised in the null mouse (P14 hippocampus, P20 tissue) and the P47T homozygote (progressive astrogliosis), and neuron-restricted rescue returns GFAP-positive cells from about 44 to about 5.

A regulator-level inflammatory signature is positive in three forebrain regions of the P47T homozygote. Without mutant animals M6 and F8 (two of five; the Nptx2 and Bdnf activity-gene signature is a post hoc designation), TNFA/NF-kB meets positive-direction q < 0.05 in no forebrain region (cortex is significantly negative) and IL6/JAK/STAT3 loses the q threshold but keeps a positive score in all three (ADV-233). [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-239: removing M6 alone also removes more than half of the TNFA set-mean rise in all three forebrain regions (left: hippocampus 0.49, cortex 0.12, prefrontal cortex 0.45 of it).]
In a seizing genetic DEE mouse (Scn1a+/-) astroglial GFAP is raised from the aggravation phase onward (abstract), a precedent that glial change in a genetic DEE can be tracked against disease stage.

A neuron-restricted deletion, whose astrocytes are expected to keep Wwox, shows astrocyte-activation-type genes among its differentially expressed genes at P17 and seizes from P9 (Repudi 2021): a glial change without an astrocyte-intrinsic lesion.
against: The rat Wwox-mutant cortex has about half the GFAP-positive and Iba1-positive cells of wild type from PND 5, the opposite sign, and the authors state it.
The human organoid shows no reactive programme, and no microglia.
Microglia carry no detectable Wwox (rat); the glial excess is therefore non-cell-autonomous for that cell type; astrocyte-specific deletion was not scored for gliosis.
The same neuron-restricted rescue that lowers GFAP also stops seizures and restores survival: the data cannot assign the fall to a glial route.

The IL-1-axis precedents are acute or post-infectious and uncontrolled or uninformative for long-term outcome: anakinra in cryptogenic NORSE/FIRES has acute seizure-control reports (up to 73 percent within two weeks in a pooled uncontrolled review of 75 patients) but long-term disability and drug-resistant epilepsy remain common and a 14-patient series shows no demonstrated long-term benefit; minocycline in chronic FIRES (three patients) is uninformative; the VX-765 phase II result is unverifiable at trial level (the registry lists a safety primary outcome and no results; the review says favorable safety and preliminary efficacy), and VX-765 had no effect in a rat infantile-spasms model.

Glial direction is context-dependent in the abstracts read: neuronal STAT3 deletion reduced glial activation and damage in neonatal hypoxia-ischaemia (Hristova 2016; astroglia-specific deletion reduced damage and microglial activation) and astrocyte uncoupling preceded seizures in a temporal-lobe-epilepsy model (Bedner 2015), so glial change can be upstream of seizures and a glial lever is not simply less gliosis; the commonly stated protective role of reactive astrocytes was not verified here.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Acute or acquired inflammation, immune-mediated syndromes and adult injury models against a congenital neuron-intrinsic loss; mouse and rat against human; null and missense WW-domain alleles against a catalytic-domain missense allele, for which no glial datum exists; chronic adult P47T against the three-week null.

p4_card.pharmacology: Not assessed: no compound is carded. Catalogue reach was measured instead (see the cycle README): the need as written reached IL1B, NLRP3, JAK2, TNF, NFKB1 and RELA but not IL1R1 or CASP1. Added from SCI's ADV-104 (class level, no dose, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE for any agent) [IT59 2026-11-20 fifth packet change]: no HE sheet covers an agent directed at microglia or inflammation, so none is carded. The two agents in HE's sheets nearest to this axis are ganaxolone and clemastine, and neither is a glia-state agent: ganaxolone has rat pharmacokinetic and intravenous titles only (no brain concentration and no juvenile or pup exposure found; in the one focal demyelination model in ovariectomised adult female rats that SCI read at passage level, microglial clearance of myelin debris and remyelination were enhanced while astrocytosis and cytokines were unaffected, a debris-clearance mechanism with no counterpart in an uninjured knockout cortex), and clemastine has a qualitative detection in juvenile rat brain and a plasma level in neonatal mouse (both from SCI's check, not re-read by HE) without a brain concentration, with an oligodendrocyte-precursor rationale rather than a glial-inflammation one.

scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: Three laboratories contribute the glial rows (Aqeilan group for the null and the AAV, Aldaz group for P47T, Suzuki group for the rat); no row is replicated by an independent laboratory in the same model.
scope_of_checks.formal_checks: The rat, null-mouse S7 and hippocampal rows were re-opened at the source on 2026-10-29 (figure and text); the P47T rows are carried from the manifest and were not re-opened except the supplementary table query. External rows are abstract level. Corrected after an independent verification on 2026-10-29.
scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Every statement marked INFERENZA, the organoid panel and every card-level synthesis, is owed a blind audit by someone other than the producer.

p4_card.predictions: Registered in the cycle README before any further data: if gliosis is a consequence of seizure-network activity, glial density in the null mouse is NOT above wild type before the first recorded spike and rises after it; if glial maturation is delayed first (the rat picture) the density is BELOW wild type before the first spike and crosses above it after seizures begin; if a neuron-derived seizure-independent signal drives it, the density is above wild type before the first spike. One time course with simultaneous recordings separates the three.
p4_card.next_measurement: Wet-lab, not done: Wwox-null (or neuron-restricted deletion) pups with wild-type littermates; GFAP and Iba1 density and area fraction in cortex and in hippocampus at P5, P8, P11, P14 and P17 on the same sections for both species-comparable readouts, with continuous cortical recording from the earliest age at which an electrode can be placed, each animal classified as before or after its first spike; controls: wild type at every age, neuron-restricted vector-treated pups; discriminating result: the sign of the glial difference before the first spike. A compound arm is not designed here. Limits: histology is terminal (one cohort per age); recording from P5 in a very small pup is a feasibility risk and onset may be as early as P9, so only about P5 to P8 are plausible pre-onset ages; a recording that starts at P14 cannot show that no earlier spike occurred. THE GLIAL AXIS IS CARRIED AS A READOUT BESIDE GLUCOSE, NOT AS AN ARM [IT59 2026-11-20 fifth packet change] (SCI's ADV-104, hypothesis level): every glial measurement in the held texts is at postnatal days 14 to 20 (area fractions of GFAP and Iba1, a few cytokine transcripts), while the earliest documented seizures are at day 9 in the neuronal-deletion line and 'within a few days after birth' in the germline null; none of the held texts measures a glial marker before the first seizure in any line, so 'not measured' is the finding, not 'not present'. SCI's condition that would promote the axis: a per-animal glial series in the neuronal-deletion cortex or the germline null at days 5, 7, 9 and 12 showing a rise before the first seizure, AND a replicated glial-state-specific manipulation that moves seizures or survival in a neuronal-primary developmental model; what would park it: gliosis first appearing at or after seizure onset in every line that reports timing, with the manipulation question still empty (no timing below day 14 has been measured by anyone, so neither condition is met today). GFAP and Iba1 are already endpoints of the gene-addition benchmark, so scoring them on the same slides of any pilot arm costs no animals.
p4_card.value_added: Replaces 'glial activation is increased in two models' by a measured conflict of sign across species with a stated discriminating design, shows the human organoid carries no reactive programme, and shows that the catalogue links of the need pointed at the wrong end of the IL-1 axis.
p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

not_known: Whether glial density in a Wwox-deficient brain is below, equal to or above wild type BEFORE the first spike.
Whether the rat and mouse signs differ by species, allele, region, assay or age window.
Whether gliosis in a Wwox-deficient brain is upstream of any measured harm.
Whether astrocyte-specific Wwox loss produces gliosis or EEG abnormality (not scored).
Any glial datum in a catalytic-domain missense allele.
Whether the unchallenged P47T heterozygote has gliosis (reported as data not shown).

Whether a glial or inflammatory state can be changed independently of neuronal rescue in the held Wwox texts [IT59 2026-11-20 fifth packet change]: the only manipulation that moves it is neuronal restoration, which moves GFAP, Iba1, survival, weight, glucose and myelination together; deletion of Wwox restricted to astrocytes or to oligodendrocyte-lineage cells gave no phenotype in the held text; in the nearest studied neuronal-primary model (Rett), one microglia-replacement report was not replicated in three models (abstract level), so the independent route is contested there and untested here.

Whether any organoid transcript difference or null on this card (deposit GSE156243) is independent of the CRISPR clone and of the batch: the sequenced knockout organoids are four of ONE clone (1B, from edit-spanning reads, ADV-244, SCI, 2026-11-25), the other clone (A2) was not sequenced, the comparator is two organoids of the parental line (the authors removed two of four wild-type libraries, one for failed quality control and one for not clustering), and the organoids appear to come from one batch (the authors' Methods: organoids from the same batch were used for all analyses unless stated otherwise; their reply to reviewers speaks of the batch of the RNA-seq; not stated as a measured fact for these six libraries), so a difference here is not shown to be a property of the knockout rather than of the clone or the batch. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-244]

Whether agreement across the P47T brain regions on this card is replication: the hippocampus, prefrontal cortex, parietal cortex and cerebellum libraries come from the same mice (five per group; cerebellum four against three), so agreement across regions is one set of animals seen several times, not replication. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-247]

Whether the hippocampal bulk contrasts on this card rest on independent animals: the arms are 2 or 3 libraries (GSE158681), one mouse per library is not stated in the sources read, and whether the same mice gave the cortices is not stated. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-247] Whatever a library contains it is at most one independent unit, so the library count is an upper bound on n; if a library is one mouse, the 2 control libraries cover at most 2 of the 4 control cortices, so the control hippocampi and cortices are not all the same mice. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-250]

The human organoid shows no reactive programme, and no microglia.
Microglia carry no detectable Wwox (rat); the glial excess is therefore non-cell-autonomous for that cell type; astrocyte-specific deletion was not scored for gliosis.
The same neuron-restricted rescue that lowers GFAP also stops seizures and restores survival: the data cannot assign the fall to a glial route.

The IL-1-axis precedents are acute or post-infectious and uncontrolled or uninformative for long-term outcome: anakinra in cryptogenic NORSE/FIRES has acute seizure-control reports (up to 73 percent within two weeks in a pooled uncontrolled review of 75 patients) but long-term disability and drug-resistant epilepsy remain common and a 14-patient series shows no demonstrated long-term benefit; minocycline in chronic FIRES (three patients) is uninformative; the VX-765 phase II result is unverifiable at trial level (the registry lists a safety primary outcome and no results; the review says favorable safety and preliminary efficacy), and VX-765 had no effect in a rat infantile-spasms model.

Glial direction is context-dependent in the abstracts read: neuronal STAT3 deletion reduced glial activation and damage in neonatal hypoxia-ischaemia (Hristova 2016; astroglia-specific deletion reduced damage and microglial activation) and astrocyte uncoupling preceded seizures in a temporal-lobe-epilepsy model (Bedner 2015), so glial change can be upstream of seizures and a glial lever is not simply less gliosis; the commonly stated protective role of reactive astrocytes was not verified here.
bridge_gaps_exposed: No drug assertion exists, so no comparison is formed.
Direction conflict between species cannot be expressed in the bridge as one comparison: the rat and mouse rows are separate assertions on different contexts.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Only IF glial reactivity is (a) real in a seizing WWOX brain, (b) not just a seizure consequence that would resolve with seizure control and (c) causally harmful rather than protective. None of the three is established. Every precedent is from acute or acquired inflammation in a normally developing brain; the WWOX lesion is congenital and neuron-intrinsic.
